- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after sentiment spikes) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for sudden rallies.  
- Model overestimates downward moves after negative sentiment — cap forecast decline at 1–3% below recent low to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- Forecast shows strong upward trend but true outcome reverses — apply mean reversion rule: if forecast > 3σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–5 days — adjust forecast to start 1–2 days earlier if sentiment is trending strongly.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) and price is rising, model underestimates — add 1–2% to forecast to capture momentum.  
- If sentiment is flat and price is falling, model overestimates — subtract 1–2% to avoid overbought sell-off.
